library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chamzas_2024_tacrolimus"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chamzas_2024_tacrolimus"))$description`
* Article: [Front Pharmacol. 2024;15:1443988](https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2024.1443988)

Chamzas et al. built a population PK model for twice-daily oral tacrolimus in
Hispanic renal transplant recipients from sparse real-world morning troughs. The
troughs alone cannot identify the absorption and distribution phases, so the
authors first fitted a two-compartment model with three Erlang transit
compartments to digitised rich profiles from the Alloway 2017 bioequivalence
trial (35 stable renal transplant recipients). They then fixed ktr, Vc/F, Vp/F,
Q/F and the between-subject variability (BSV) on each, and estimated only CL/F,
its BSV, the hematocrit effect and the residual error from the sparse Hispanic
data. Body weight scales all four disposition parameters allometrically
(Equations 5-8).

# Population

The final model was fitted to 121 self-identified Hispanic adult renal
allograft recipients transplanted at St. Joseph Hospital (Orange, California)
between 2008 and 2020, with 2,215 morning tacrolimus troughs from the first 30
days of therapy (Results, Figure 1). Table 1 of the source reports 61% male, age
45.7 (SD 12.9) years, weight 77.3 (SD 20.1) kg, BMI 27.6 (SD 5.2) kg/m^2 and
hematocrit 30.0 (SD 4.9)%. 87% were first transplants and 71% had deceased
donors. All patients received thymoglobulin induction, a corticosteroid taper
and mycophenolate mofetil. Initial tacrolimus doses ranged from 0.02 to 0.14
mg/kg/day (median 0.06 mg/kg/day) and were titrated to a 10-12 ng/mL trough
target. Concentrations were measured in whole blood by LC-MS/MS.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Chamzas_2024_tacrolimus")()$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Chamzas_2024_tacrolimus.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL/F, 70 kg, HCT 30%) | log(13.65) L/h | Table 2 (RSE 4.32%); Abstract '13.7 L/h' |
| `lvc` (Vc/F, 70 kg) | fixed(log(171)) L | Table 2; Results 3.1 |
| `lvp` (Vp/F, 70 kg) | fixed(log(325.6)) L | Results 3.1 '325.6 L' (Table 2 prints 325) |
| `lq` (Q/F, 70 kg) | fixed(log(62.46)) L/h | Table 2 (Results 3.1 '62.5 L/h') |
| `lktr` | fixed(log(4.27)) 1/h | Table 2; Results 3.1 |
| `e_wt_cl_q` | fixed(0.75) | Equations 5 and 8 |
| `e_wt_vc_vp` | fixed(1) | Equations 6 and 7 |
| `e_hct_cl` | -0.83 | Table 2 HCTcov = 0.83 (RSE 8.46%), negative sign from Equation 5 |
| `etalcl` | 0.4700 | Table 2 %BSV 77.46 -> log(1 + 0.7746^2) |
| `etalvc` | fixed(0.8800) | Table 2 %BSV 118.78 (fixed) |
| `etalvp` | fixed(0.7140) | Table 2 %BSV 102.09 (fixed) |
| `etalq` | fixed(0.7550) | Table 2 %BSV 106.19 (fixed) |
| `etalktr` | fixed(0.5580) | Table 2 %BSV 86.44 (fixed) |
| `addSd` | 2.62 ng/mL | Table 2 RUV additive (RSE 12.85%) |
| CL/F equation | `tvcl * (HCT/30)^-0.83 * (WT/70)^0.75 * exp(eta)` | Equation 5; Table 2 footnote |
| Vc/F, Vp/F, Q/F, ktr equations | as in model | Equations 6-9 |
| Two-compartment disposition, 3 transit compartments | n/a | Results 3.1; Supplementary Table S1 |

## Covariate fold-changes (Supplementary Table S2)

Supplementary Table S2 reports how CL/F changes relative to the typical
patient (70 kg, 30% hematocrit). These are closed-form functions of the
packaged parameters.

```{r supp-table-s2}
mod <- readModelDb("Chamzas_2024_tacrolimus")
th <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)$theta

s2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~covariate,     ~WT, ~HCT, ~published,
  "WT = 45 kg",    45,   30,  0.7,
  "WT = 160 kg",  160,   30,  1.8,
  "HCT = 15%",     70,   15,  1.7,
  "HCT = 50%",     70,   50,  0.7
) |>
  mutate(
    model = (HCT / 30)^th[["e_hct_cl"]] * (WT / 70)^th[["e_wt_cl_q"]]
  )

s2 |>
  rename(
    "Covariate value" = covariate,
    "Published fold-change" = published,
    "Model fold-change" = model
  ) |>
  select(-WT, -HCT) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "CL/F relative to a 70 kg patient with 30% hematocrit.")

# The paper prints one decimal and truncates rather than rounds (1.86 -> 1.8,
# 1.78 -> 1.7), so a 0.1 tolerance is the resolution of the printed table.
stopifnot(all(abs(s2$model - s2$published) < 0.1 + 1e-9))
```

# Virtual cohort

The observed data are not public. The virtual cohort draws body weight and
hematocrit from normal distributions with the Table 1 means and SDs, truncated
to plausible ranges. Each patient keeps one hematocrit for the simulation.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20241001)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241001)

n_per_arm <- 200L
covs <- tibble(
  WT = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_per_arm, 77.3, 20.1), 40), 160),
  HCT = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_per_arm, 30.0, 4.9), 15), 50)
)

# Twice-daily oral doses of `mgkgday / 2` mg/kg, rounded to the 0.5 mg
# capsule increment the authors used, and morning troughs every 24 h.
# The same covariates are reused in every arm so that arms differ only in dose.
make_arm <- function(mgkgday, id_offset, obs_times = seq(24, 144, by = 24)) {
  subj <- covs |>
    mutate(id = id_offset + seq_len(n()), arm = sprintf("%.2f", mgkgday))
  doses <- subj |>
    tidyr::expand_grid(time = seq(0, 13 * 12, by = 12)) |>
    mutate(
      evid = 1L,
      amt = pmax(0.5, round(WT * mgkgday / 2 / 0.5) * 0.5),
      cmt = "depot"
    )
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::expand_grid(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

initial_doses <- c(0.06, 0.07, 0.08, 0.09, 0.10, 0.11, 0.12)
events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(initial_doses), function(i) {
  make_arm(initial_doses[i], id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

The full population model, with between-subject variability (BSV) on every
parameter, is solved on the event table above. `Cc` is the individual
prediction without residual error, matching how the authors' dose-finding
simulations were run.

```{r simulate}
troughs <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("arm", "WT", "HCT")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(day = time / 24)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 5: troughs on days 2 and 3 by initial dose

The source labels the morning troughs as Day 2 and Day 3. The simulated troughs
at 48 h and 72 h after the first dose reproduce the published medians. The
medians below were digitised by the maintainers from the Figure 5 box plots
(about +/- 0.4 ng/mL reading resolution).

```{r figure-5}
fig5_published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,   ~day, ~published_median,
  "0.07", 2,    6.5,
  "0.08", 2,    7.4,
  "0.09", 2,    8.2,
  "0.10", 2,    9.2,
  "0.11", 2,   10.2,
  "0.12", 2,   10.8,
  "0.07", 3,    7.8,
  "0.08", 3,    9.3,
  "0.09", 3,   10.5,
  "0.10", 3,   11.6,
  "0.11", 3,   12.5,
  "0.12", 3,   13.6
)

fig5_sim <- troughs |>
  filter(day %in% c(2, 3), arm != "0.06") |>
  mutate(day = factor(day))

ggplot(fig5_sim, aes(day, Cc, fill = arm)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(10, 12), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Day", y = "Tacrolimus trough (ng/mL)", fill = "Initial dose\n(mg/kg/day)",
    title = "Figure 5: troughs on days 2 and 3 by initial dose",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Chamzas 2024."
  )

fig5_cmp <- troughs |>
  filter(day %in% c(2, 3), arm != "0.06") |>
  group_by(arm, day) |>
  summarise(sim_median = median(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(fig5_published, by = c("arm", "day")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim_median - published_median) / published_median)

fig5_cmp |>
  select(day, arm, published_median, sim_median, pct_diff) |>
  arrange(day, arm) |>
  rename(
    "Day" = day, "Initial dose (mg/kg/day)" = arm,
    "Published median (ng/mL)" = published_median,
    "Simulated median (ng/mL)" = sim_median, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Median trough: simulation vs. digitised Figure 5.")

stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-transcribed CL/F, volume or dose unit shifts every arm
  # by tens of percent. Typical-value troughs (every eta at zero) run 20-30%
  # above these medians, because the large BSV on Vc/F, Vp/F, Q/F and ktr
  # pulls the median trough below the typical-value trough.
  abs(median(fig5_cmp$pct_diff)) < 10,
  # Envelope across the twelve arm-days, robust to the cohort draw.
  quantile(abs(fig5_cmp$pct_diff), 0.9) < 25
)
```

The simulated spread for 0.10 mg/kg/day on day 3 is somewhat wider than the
published box (about 8-15.5 ng/mL in Figure 5). The source reports that 27% of
patients were inside 10-12 ng/mL and 18% were above 15 ng/mL on day 3 at this
dose (Results 3.3.1). Those proportions come from the cohort's own post-hoc
parameters and covariates, so a virtual cohort is not expected to reproduce
them exactly.

```{r figure-5-spread}
troughs |>
  filter(arm == "0.10", day == 3) |>
  summarise(
    p25 = quantile(Cc, 0.25), median = median(Cc), p75 = quantile(Cc, 0.75),
    pct_10_12 = 100 * mean(Cc >= 10 & Cc <= 12),
    pct_above_15 = 100 * mean(Cc > 15)
  ) |>
  rename(
    "P25 (ng/mL)" = p25, "Median (ng/mL)" = median, "P75 (ng/mL)" = p75,
    "% in 10-12 ng/mL" = pct_10_12, "% above 15 ng/mL" = pct_above_15
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated day-3 troughs at 0.10 mg/kg/day.")
```

## Figure 3: trough at 72 h

The quantitative predictive check (Figure 3) compares the median observed trough
in the 66-74 h window (about 8.3 ng/mL) with the median of 1,000 simulated
datasets (about 8.7 ng/mL; median prediction error +5.01%). The patients in
that window received their recorded doses: initial doses ranged from 0.02 to
0.14 mg/kg/day (median 0.06), and some had already been adjusted by 72 h. The
closest virtual counterpart is the untitrated 0.06 mg/kg/day arm. It is shown
for orientation only and is not used as a check, because its median runs 10-25%
below 8.7 ng/mL across cohort draws. The dose history behind the published
window is not available.

```{r figure-3}
qpc <- troughs |>
  filter(arm == "0.06", time == 72) |>
  summarise(median_trough = median(Cc))
knitr::kable(
  rename(qpc, "Simulated median trough at 72 h (ng/mL)" = median_trough),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Median 72-h trough, untitrated 0.06 mg/kg/day; published observed median 8.3 ng/mL, simulated 8.7 ng/mL."
)
```

## Figures 6-8: titration strategies

Figures 6 and 7 apply the recommended titration protocol in Table 3. Figure 8
applies the hospital's current titration protocol, which the source does not
publish. Neither is reproduced here, because both depend on per-patient
post-hoc parameters and on scheduling rules that the source does not fully
specify, such as when a measured trough triggers an adjustment, and on which
day the adjusted dose is next re-measured.

# PKNCA validation

The source reports no NCA. This check confirms internal consistency at steady
state. Over one 12-h dosing interval, AUC0-12 must equal Dose / (CL/F) for each
subject. Doses are given at steady state (`ss = 1`) and sampled on a dense grid.

```{r pknca}
nca_events <- bind_rows(lapply(c(0.06, 0.10), function(d) {
  covs |>
    slice_head(n = 100) |>
    mutate(
      id = seq_len(n()) + if (d == 0.06) 0L else 100L,
      treatment = sprintf("%.2f mg/kg/day", d),
      amt = pmax(0.5, round(WT * d / 2 / 0.5) * 0.5)
    )
})) |>
  (\(subj) bind_rows(
    subj |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, ss = 1L, ii = 12, cmt = "depot"),
    subj |>
      tidyr::expand_grid(obs_time = seq(0, 12, by = 0.1)) |>
      mutate(time = obs_time, evid = 0L, amt = 0, ss = 0L, ii = 0, cmt = "central") |>
      select(-obs_time)
  ))() |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = nca_events, keep = c("treatment")) |>
  as.data.frame()

conc_df <- sim_ss |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- nca_events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 12,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  select(treatment, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

nca_wide |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    cmax = median(cmax), tmax = median(tmax), cmin = median(cmin),
    auclast = median(auclast), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(
    "Regimen" = treatment, "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "Cmin (ng/mL)" = cmin, "AUC0-12 (ng*h/mL)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Steady-state NCA (medians across subjects).")

# AUC0-12 at steady state = Dose / (CL/F); mg / (L/h) * 1000 = ng*h/mL.
auc_chk <- sim_ss |>
  distinct(id, cl) |>
  inner_join(distinct(dose_df, id, amt), by = "id") |>
  inner_join(nca_wide, by = "id") |>
  mutate(pct_err = 100 * (auclast - amt * 1000 / cl) / (amt * 1000 / cl))
stopifnot(
  # Same drawn parameters on both sides: only trapezoid error on a 0.1 h grid
  # (observed 90th percentile about 0.005% across cohort draws).
  abs(median(auc_chk$pct_err)) < 0.1,
  quantile(abs(auc_chk$pct_err), 0.9) < 0.5
)
summary(auc_chk$pct_err)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Transit chain.** The source states that "three transit compartments" fit
  the rich data and reports only one rate constant (Ktr), with no separate
  absorption rate. The package follows the reading used for the Benkali 2010
  and Woillard 2011 tacrolimus models (both cited by the source as the same
  structure): the dose enters the first of three compartments, and each
  compartment, including the last, transfers at ktr. An alternative reading,
  with three transit compartments after a separate dosing depot (four transfers
  at ktr), changes the simulated typical troughs at 0.1 mg/kg/day by less than
  1% and the steady-state Cmax by less than 0.5%. The maintainers checked both
  readings, and the difference is immaterial for this trough-based model.
- **BSV scale.** Table 2 reports %BSV without a definition. The variances are
  taken as `log(1 + (%BSV/100)^2)`. This gives the round values 0.470, 0.880,
  0.714, 0.755 and 0.558, which suggests the authors reported the
  exponential-scale CV of round omega^2 values. Reading %BSV as sqrt(omega^2)
  instead would give variances of 0.60 to 1.41.
- **Vp/F and Q/F precision.** Results 3.1 gives Vp/F = 325.6 L and Q/F = 62.5
  L/h, while Table 2 gives 325 L and 62.46 L/h. The more precise value of each
  is used.
- **Hematocrit reference.** Equation 5 centres hematocrit on "HCT_median"
  without printing the number. The Abstract and Supplementary Table S2 name the
  typical patient as having 30% hematocrit, and Table 1 reports a cohort mean of
  30.0%. The model uses 30%, which reproduces all four Supplementary Table S2
  fold-changes.
- **Hematocrit is time-varying in the source.** The virtual cohort holds each
  patient's hematocrit constant. Supply HCT per record (in percent) to simulate
  its post-transplant recovery.
- **Bioavailability.** All disposition parameters are apparent (divided by F),
  and no bioavailability term is carried.
- **Residual error.** Table 2 reports an additive residual error only (2.62
  ng/mL). The simulations above use individual predictions without residual
  error, as the source did for its dose-finding simulations.
- **Virtual cohort.** Weight and hematocrit are drawn from normal distributions
  with the Table 1 means and SDs, truncated to 40-160 kg and 15-50%, and drawn
  independently of each other.
- **Not reproduced.** The titration-protocol simulations (Figures 6-8) are
  described above. The source reports no NCA, so the PKNCA section checks
  internal steady-state consistency instead of comparing against published
  values.
- Europe PMC lists no erratum or correction notice for this article as of
  2026-10-30.
